rules.name: Dec
rules.cases: K(h;P;T) = 0^inf <D (10)^h 11001 [p_1,q_1,d_1]...[p_L,q_L,d_L] T 0^inf, [p,q,d] = (10)^p (01)^q s(d), s(1)=0001, s(0)=0010. Z = pairs below the first d=1, all d=0, q>=2; touch (p,q,d) = (p+1,q-1,1-d). #3's rule with <A read as <D

rules.name: DecMerge
rules.cases: q runs out on the 1->0 digit: fuse with the next pair

rules.name: DecMergeTail
rules.cases: the last pair runs out into the T1 tail

rules.name: DecMergeEmpty
rules.cases: the last pair runs out, no tail (never on the orbit)

rules.name: End
rules.cases: V = 0, no tail: adds tail T1(1)

rules.name: EndLast
rules.cases: V = 0, last q = 1: last pair becomes the tail

rules.name: Ov
rules.cases: V = 0 with tail: re-pairing (q_j, p_{j+1}), one more pair, h back to 2

rules.name: X1
rules.cases: V = 0, last two q = 1: re-pairing with tail T2

rules.name: X2
rules.cases: V = 0 with tail T2: End-like, appends pair (3,k+1,1)

zoom_cycles_annotated: each row is the tape at the start of one count-down step. A pair = a run of 10s (blue) then a run of 01s (orange); its digit block = the next 4 cells (purple), 0001 = 1, 0010 = 0. Re-pairing (the yellow bands, above rows 6,965 and 17,738) = the tape is regrouped into new pairs and the counter (right margin) restarts, at 6, then at 2; it happens at the counter's second 0. At the first 0 the step is End instead: it raises the counter (0 → 1 at row 5,100; 0 → 3 at row 12,389; 0 → 1 at row 20,870) and changes the right end: '+ tail' adds a 3-cell teal tail after the last pair, 'pair 3 → tail' absorbs pair 3 into the tail. (a) Between the bands: each purple block stays in the same 4 columns; only the 1 inside it moves, 0010 ↔ 0001 (pair 3 becomes the teal tail at row 12,389, pair 2 joins it at row 14,453). The blue→orange borders jump 2 cells right: pair 1's on every row, pair 2's on every other row (the magnified box at the top shows one such step). (b) At each band: the black dashed lines (old borders) end on the new purple blocks, and the purple dotted lines (middles of the old purple blocks) end 1 cell left of the new borders (pair 1's starts next to the old gold marker), so the two kinds of column swap roles. The added pair (2 → 3 pairs, then 1 → 2) has its orange run over the old teal tail and its purple block (the rightmost) just past the tail's end, so no line leads to it. Is (a) what you see? Is (b)? (In init_recL_4e4 the edges kink at each swap.)
OK to submit with the 3-pair base after re-pairing 6, rather than the 4-pair E-start after re-pairing 8 (step 104,510)?
